title.raw: 卷143 志一百十八 刑法二

sentences.zh: 志一百十八

translations.literal: Treatise 118
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Number 118

sentences.zh: 刑法二

translations.literal: Penal Law II
translations.idiomatic: Penal Law, Part Two

sentences.zh: 明律淵源唐代，以笞、杖、徒、流、死為五刑。

translations.literal: Ming penal law traced its origins to the Tang dynasty, taking beating with the light stick, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, exile, and death as the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming code descended from Tang law and recognized five standard punishments: disciplinary beating, heavier beating, penal servitude, exile, and death.

sentences.zh: 自笞一十至五十，為笞刑五。

translations.literal: From ten blows of the light stick to fifty constituted the five grades of beating with the light stick.
translations.idiomatic: Light-stick beating ran in five steps from ten to fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 自杖六十至一百，為杖刑五。

translations.literal: From sixty blows of the heavy stick to one hundred constituted the five grades of beating with the heavy stick.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy-stick beating ran in five steps from sixty to one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒自杖六十徒一年起，每等加杖十，刑期半年，至杖一百徒三年，為徒五等。

translations.literal: Penal servitude began with sixty blows of the heavy stick and one year of servitude; each grade added ten blows, with the term of punishment increased by half a year, up to one hundred blows and three years of servitude, making five grades of penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude started at sixty strokes of the cane plus one year's labor; each step up added ten strokes and six months to the term, culminating at one hundred strokes and three years—five grades in all.

sentences.zh: 流以二千里、二千五百里、三千里為三等，而皆加杖一百。

translations.literal: Exile had three grades at two thousand li, two thousand five hundred li, and three thousand li, each with an additional one hundred blows of the heavy stick.
translations.idiomatic: Exile came in three distances—two thousand, two thousand five hundred, and three thousand li—with one hundred heavy strokes added in every case.

sentences.zh: 死刑二：曰斬，曰絞。

translations.literal: There were two forms of death penalty: decapitation and strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment had two forms: beheading and strangulation.

sentences.zh: 此正刑也。

translations.literal: These were the regular punishments.
translations.idiomatic: These constituted the standard punishments.

sentences.zh: 其律例內之雜犯、斬絞、遷徙、充軍、枷號、刺字、論贖、凌遲、梟首、戮屍等刑，或取諸前代，或明所自創，要皆非刑之正。

translations.literal: Among punishments within the statutes and precedents—miscellaneous offenses, decapitation and strangulation, relocation, military banishment, wearing the cangue, tattooing, commutation by ransom, lingchi, exposure of the head, and dismemberment of the corpse—some were taken from earlier dynasties and some were innovations of the Ming; all were essentially not among the regular punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and subsidiary rules also prescribed punishments such as miscellaneous offenses, special beheading and strangulation, relocation, military exile, cangue detention, tattooing, ransom conversion, lingchi, displaying the head, and corpse mutilation—some borrowed from earlier ages, some invented under the Ming—all of them outside the five regular punishments.

sentences.zh: 清太祖、太宗之治遼東，刑制尚簡，重則斬，輕則鞭撲而已。

translations.literal: Under the Taizu and Taizong emperors in governing the Eastern Liao, the penal system was still simple: serious cases were punished by decapitation, light ones by whipping and beating only.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing founders ruled the Eastern Liao, penal practice remained austere—capital cases ended in decapitation, minor ones in lashes and beatings, and little else.

sentences.zh: 迨世祖入關，沿襲明制，初頒刑律，笞、杖以五折十，注入本刑各條。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the Pass, he followed the Ming system; when the penal code was first promulgated, beating with the light and heavy sticks was calculated at five-tenths of ten, inserted into each article of the principal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi emperor crossed into China proper, the dynasty adopted Ming practice; the first Qing code reduced light- and heavy-stick counts to half the Ming scale (the "five-tenths of ten" rule), embedding the figures in each statutory article.

sentences.zh: 康熙朝現行則例改為四折除零。

translations.literal: The operative regulations of the Kangxi reign changed this to four-tenths with remainders dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, the living regulations further cut the rate to four-tenths, discarding fractional strokes.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，乃依例各於本律註明板數。

translations.literal: The code of the third year of the Yongzheng reign, following precedent, noted the number of blows in each principal statute.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng code of 1725 fixed the actual stroke counts in the text of each statute, as precedents required.

sentences.zh: 徒、流加杖，亦至配所照數折責。

translations.literal: Additional beating for penal servitude and exile was likewise reduced according to the count upon arrival at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Supplementary strokes for servitude and exile were also discounted to the prescribed figure once the convict reached his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐撲責過多，致傷生命，法外之仁也。

translations.literal: This was because they feared that excessive beating and flogging would injure life—a mercy beyond the letter of the law.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to keep flogging from becoming so severe that it endangered the convict's life—a humane allowance beyond strict legal form.

sentences.zh: 文武官犯笞、杖，則分別公私，代以罰俸、降級、降調，至革職而止。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials committed offenses warranting beating with the light or heavy stick, public and private cases were distinguished, and salary fines, demotion in rank, transfer to a lower post, up to dismissal from office, were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials sentenced to light- or heavy-stick beating were treated differently for public and private offenses, paying fines in lieu of salary, suffering demotion or reassignment, or losing their posts altogether—never the physical blows themselves.

sentences.zh: 徒者，奴也，蓋奴辱之。

translations.literal: Penal servitude means "slave," for it was essentially enslavement and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The character for penal servitude means "slave," and the punishment was meant to reduce the offender to servile shame.

sentences.zh: 明發鹽場鐵冶煎鹽炒鐵，清則發本省驛遞。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, convicts were sent to salt works and iron smelteries to boil salt and smelt iron; under the Qing they were sent to courier stations within their own province.
translations.idiomatic: Ming convicts labored at salt pans and ironworks; Qing convicts served on the provincial relay network.

sentences.zh: 其無驛縣，分撥各衙門充水火夫各項雜役，限滿釋放。

translations.literal: Where there were no courier counties, they were assigned among various yamens as water carriers, fire tenders, and other miscellaneous laborers, and released when the term expired.
translations.idiomatic: Counties without relay stations distributed convicts among government offices as water carriers, stokers, and other menial hands, releasing them when their terms ended.

sentences.zh: 流犯，初制由各縣解交巡撫衙門，按照里數，酌發各處荒蕪及瀕海州縣。

translations.literal: For exiled convicts, the initial system was for each county to deliver them to the provincial governor's yamen, which, according to the distance in li, assigned them to various desolate or coastal prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At first, counties forwarded exiles to the provincial governor, who sent them to wasteland or coastal districts according to the statutory distance.

sentences.zh: 嗣以各省分撥失均，不免趨避揀擇。

translations.literal: Later, because allocation among provinces was uneven, evasion and cherry-picking could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Uneven provincial quotas soon led officials and convicts alike to game assignments and avoid the harshest destinations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，刑部始纂輯三流道里表，將某省某府屬流犯，應流二千里者發何省何府屬安置，應流二千五百里者發何省何府屬安置，應流三千里者發何省何府屬安置，按計程途，限定地址，逐省逐府，分別開載。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Qianlong reign, the Ministry of Justice first compiled tables of routes and distances for the three grades of exile, listing for convicts from such-and-such a province and prefecture who should be exiled two thousand li which province and prefecture they should be sent to for resettlement, likewise for two thousand five hundred li and three thousand li, calculating the journey, fixing the address, and opening entries province by province and prefecture by prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1743 the Ministry of Justice compiled route tables for all three exile distances, specifying for every originating province and prefecture exactly which receiving province and prefecture would take convicts sentenced to two thousand, two thousand five hundred, or three thousand li—mileage calculated, destinations fixed, and each line entered in the register.

sentences.zh: 嗣於四十九年及嘉慶六年兩次修訂。

translations.literal: It was twice revised in the forty-ninth year of his reign and in the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign.
translations.idiomatic: The tables were revised twice, in 1784 and 1801.

sentences.zh: 然第於州縣之增並，道里之參差，略有修改，而大體不易。

translations.literal: Yet only with respect to the annexation or merger of prefectures and counties and discrepancies in routes and distances were there slight modifications; the overall scheme did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Later edits adjusted only for merged districts and shifted mileages; the overall allocation scheme stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 律稱：「犯流妻妾從之，父祖子孫欲隨者聽。

translations.literal: The code states: "When one is exiled, wives and concubines follow; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wish to accompany may do so."
translations.idiomatic: Statute provided that a convict's wives and concubines must accompany him into exile, and that parents, grandparents, children, and grandchildren might follow if they chose.

sentences.zh: 」乾隆二十四年，將僉妻之例停止。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-fourth year of the Qianlong reign, the precedent requiring wives to accompany was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1759 the compulsory accompaniment of wives was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其軍、流、遣犯情原隨帶家屬者，不得官為資送，律成虛設矣。

translations.literal: As for military exiles, exiles, and banished convicts who in principle wished to bring their families, the state no longer provided transport—so the statute became a dead letter.
translations.idiomatic: Military exiles, ordinary exiles, and banished convicts who wished to take dependents along received no official escort or support, and the statutory family provisions became meaningless.

sentences.zh: 斬、絞，同是死刑。

translations.literal: Decapitation and strangulation are alike death penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Beheading and strangulation were both forms of capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 然自漢以來，有秋後決囚之制。

translations.literal: Yet since the Han dynasty there has been the system of executing prisoners after autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times, however, capital sentences were normally carried out only after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 唐律除犯惡逆以上及奴婢、部曲殺主者，從立春至秋分不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: Tang law, except for those guilty of treason and the like and for slaves, retainers, and dependent households who killed their masters, forbade reporting capital cases for decision from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Tang law barred execution between spring and autumn except for the gravest treason and for slaves or dependents who murdered their masters.

sentences.zh: 明弘治十年奏定真犯死罪決不待時者，凌遲十二條，斬三十七條，絞十二條；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, it was memorialized and fixed that for true capital offenses to be executed without waiting for the season: lingchi twelve articles, decapitation thirty-seven articles, strangulation twelve articles;
translations.idiomatic: In 1497 the Ming court listed capital offenses to be executed immediately: twelve calling for lingchi, thirty-seven for decapitation, and twelve for strangulation;

sentences.zh: 真犯死罪秋後處決者，斬一百條，絞八十六條。

translations.literal: for true capital offenses to be executed after autumn: decapitation one hundred articles, strangulation eighty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: and those held for autumn execution: one hundred decapitations and eighty-six strangulations.

sentences.zh: 順治初定律，乃於各條內分晰註明，凡律不注監候者，皆立決也；

translations.literal: When the code was first fixed in the early Shunzhi reign, each article was clearly annotated within it: wherever the statute did not note imprisonment awaiting review, all were immediate execution;
translations.idiomatic: The early Shunzhi code marked each article explicitly: any statute that did not say "imprisonment awaiting review" meant immediate execution;

sentences.zh: 凡例不言立決者，皆監候也。

translations.literal: wherever a subsidiary rule did not speak of immediate execution, all were imprisonment awaiting review.
translations.idiomatic: and any subsidiary rule that did not specify immediate execution meant imprisonment awaiting autumn review.

sentences.zh: 自此京、外死罪多決於秋，朝審遂為一代之大典。

translations.literal: From this time onward most capital cases in the capital and in the provinces were decided in autumn, and the autumn court review became a great institution of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter most death sentences in the capital and provinces were settled in autumn, and the autumn judicial review became one of the dynasty's defining institutions.

sentences.zh: 雜犯斬、絞准徒五年與雜犯三流總徒四年，大都創自有明。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous offenses of decapitation and strangulation commuted to five years of penal servitude, and miscellaneous offenses of the three grades of exile totaling four years of penal servitude, were largely innovations of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Commuting miscellaneous capital offenses to five years' servitude and the three exile grades to four years' servitude were largely Ming inventions.

sentences.zh: 清律於官吏受贓，枉法不枉法，滿貫俱改為實絞，餘多仍之。

translations.literal: The Qing code, for officials and clerks receiving bribes, whether perverting the law or not, when the full quota was reached all changed to actual strangulation; most of the rest were retained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing code made full-scale official bribery—whether or not the law was perverted—actual strangulation rather than imprisonment awaiting review, while leaving most other Ming provisions intact.

sentences.zh: 名實混淆，殊形轇轕。

translations.literal: Names and realities were confused, and the forms became tangled indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Labels and punishments no longer matched, and the system grew hopelessly entangled.

sentences.zh: 遷徙原於唐之殺人移鄉，而定罪則異。

translations.literal: Relocation derived from the Tang practice of moving murderers to another district, but the determination of guilt differed.
translations.idiomatic: Relocation traced back to the Tang custom of banishing killers to another district, though the Qing defined the offense differently.

sentences.zh: 律文沿用數條，然皆改為比流減半、徒二年，並不徙諸千里之外。

translations.literal: Several articles of the code were retained, yet all were changed to half the distance of exile and two years of penal servitude, and did not relocate people a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: A few statutory articles survived, but all were recast as half the statutory exile distance plus two years' servitude—never a thousand-li banishment.

sentences.zh: 惟條例於土蠻、瑤、僮、苗人仇殺劫擄及改土為流之土司有犯，將家口實行遷徙。

translations.literal: Only in subsidiary rules, for native chiefs of the Tuman, Yao, Zhuang, and Miao who committed feud killing, plunder, and abduction, and for tusi who had their domains converted to regular administration and then offended, were households actually relocated.
translations.idiomatic: Subsidiary rules alone required whole households to be moved when tribal leaders among the Tuman, Yao, Zhuang, or Miao committed feud murders, raids, or kidnappings, or when former native chiefs whose domains had been regularized broke the law.

sentences.zh: 然各有定地，亦不限千里也。

translations.literal: Yet each had a fixed place, and was likewise not limited to a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Each case had a designated destination, but again without the thousand-li limit.

sentences.zh: 明之充軍，義主實邊，不盡與流刑相比附。

translations.literal: Ming military banishment was chiefly meant to strengthen the frontier and was not entirely comparable to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, military banishment was meant to reinforce the borders and did not map neatly onto ordinary exile.

sentences.zh: 清初裁撤邊衛，而仍沿充軍之名。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, frontier garrisons were abolished, yet the name of military banishment was retained.
translations.idiomatic: The early Qing abolished frontier garrisons but kept the term "military banishment."

sentences.zh: 後遂以附近、近邊、邊遠、極邊、煙瘴為五軍，且於滿流以上，為節級加等之用。

translations.literal: Later there came to be five military categories—nearby, near frontier, distant frontier, extreme frontier, and miasmic regions—and for full exile and above they served to moderate and add grades of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades emerged—nearby, near border, distant border, extreme border, and miasmic regions—used to step punishments up or down from full exile.

sentences.zh: 附近二千里，近邊二千五百里，邊遠三千里，極邊、煙瘴俱四千里。

translations.literal: Nearby was two thousand li, near frontier two thousand five hundred li, distant frontier three thousand li, extreme frontier and miasmic regions both four thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby meant two thousand li, near border two thousand five hundred, distant border three thousand, and both extreme border and miasmic regions four thousand.

sentences.zh: 在京兵部定地，在外巡撫定地。

translations.literal: In the capital the Ministry of War fixed the place; in the provinces the governor-general or governor fixed the place.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War assigned destinations for convicts from the capital; provincial governors did so elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，第於十五布政司應發省分約略編定。

translations.literal: The code of the third year of the Yongzheng reign only roughly compiled which provinces the fifteen provincial administrations should send convicts to.
translations.idiomatic: The 1725 code only roughly listed which provinces should receive convicts from each of the fifteen provincial administrations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，兵部根據邦政紀略，輯為五軍道里表，凡發配者，視表所列。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign, the Ministry of War, based on the Summary of Border Administration, compiled tables of routes and distances for the five military categories; all who were sent into banishment followed what the tables listed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772 the Ministry of War, drawing on border-administration records, compiled route tables for all five military grades, and every banishment followed the listed assignment.

sentences.zh: 然名為充軍，至配並不入營差操，第於每月朔望檢點，實與流犯無異。

translations.literal: Yet though called military banishment, upon assignment they did not enter camps for duty and drill, but were only inspected on the first and fifteenth of each month—in reality no different from exiled convicts.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the name, banished convicts never joined garrison rolls or drill; they were checked only on the first and fifteenth of each month—in practice indistinguishable from ordinary exiles.

sentences.zh: 而滿流加附近、近邊道里，反由遠而近，司讞者每苦其紛歧，而又有發遣名目。

translations.literal: Yet when full exile was increased to nearby and near-frontier distances, the routes went from distant to near, and those who judged cases were often troubled by the confusion; moreover there was the category of banishment dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Adding nearby and near-border distances on top of full exile reversed the logic of distance, baffling judicial officers—and then there was the separate category of "banishment dispatch."

sentences.zh: 初第發尚陽堡、寧古塔，或烏喇地方安插，後並發齊齊哈爾、黑龍江、三姓、喀爾喀、科布多，或各省駐防為奴。

translations.literal: At first they were sent only to Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or resettled in the Ula region; later they were also sent to Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or made slaves at garrisons in various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At first convicts went only to Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or the Ula region; later also to Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or into bondage at provincial garrisons.

sentences.zh: 乾隆年間，新疆開闢，例又有發往伊犁、烏魯木齊、巴里坤各回城分別為奴種地者。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, when Xinjiang was opened, precedents also provided for sending convicts to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and various Muslim cities to be slaves who cleared and farmed land.
translations.idiomatic: After Xinjiang was opened in the Qianlong era, precedents also sent convicts to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and Muslim towns as bondsmen to clear and farm the land.

sentences.zh: 咸、同之際，新疆道梗，又復改發內地充軍。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng and Tongzhi periods, when routes to Xinjiang were blocked, banishment was again changed to military exile within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the routes to Xinjiang were cut during the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, convicts were again sent to military exile inside China proper.

sentences.zh: 其制屢經變易，然軍遣止及其身。

translations.literal: The system changed repeatedly, yet military banishment and dispatch applied only to the person himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rules shifted often, but military banishment and dispatch punished only the convict himself.

sentences.zh: 苟情節稍輕，尚得更赦放還。

translations.literal: If the circumstances were somewhat lighter, they might still obtain amnesty and be released to return.
translations.idiomatic: Lighter cases could still win amnesty and return home.

sentences.zh: 以視明之永遠軍戍，數世後猶句及本籍子孫者，大有間也。

translations.literal: Compared with the Ming's perpetual military garrison service, in which generations later descendants in their native place were still implicated, there was a great difference.
translations.idiomatic: This was a far cry from the Ming practice of perpetual frontier service, which could still entangle a convict's descendants in his home district generations later.

sentences.zh: 若文武職官犯徒以上，輕則軍台效力，重則新疆當差。

translations.literal: If civil and military officials committed offenses above penal servitude, in lighter cases they served at relay stations; in heavier cases they performed duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials guilty of more than penal servitude served lightly at relay stations or, in serious cases, at labor in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 成案相沿，遂為定例。

translations.literal: As precedents accumulated, this became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated case law turned the practice into fixed precedent.

sentences.zh: 此又軍遣中之歧出者焉。

translations.literal: This was yet another exceptional branch within military banishment and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: This was yet another special variant within military banishment and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 枷杻，本以羈獄囚。

translations.literal: The cangue and fetters were originally used to restrain prisoners in jail.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue and shackles were originally tools for restraining jail prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明代問刑條例，於本罪外或加以枷號，示戮辱也。

translations.literal: The Ming regulations on interrogation and punishment sometimes added wearing the cangue beyond the principal offense, to display shame and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Ming interrogation regulations sometimes added cangue time beyond the principal sentence as public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 清律犯罪免發遣條：「凡旗人犯罪，笞、杖各照數鞭責，軍、流、徒免發遣，分別枷號。

translations.literal: The Qing statute on offenses exempt from banishment states: "Whenever a Bannerman commits an offense, for beating with the light or heavy stick he is flogged according to the number; for military banishment, exile, or penal servitude he is exempt from dispatch and instead wears the cangue for a set period."
translations.idiomatic: The Qing statute on exempt offenses reads: "Bannermen who commit crimes receive the full light- or heavy-stick flogging; for military banishment, exile, or penal servitude they are not sent away but wear the cangue instead."

sentences.zh: 徒一年者，枷號二十日，每等遞加五日。

translations.literal: For one year of penal servitude, wearing the cangue twenty days; each grade adds five days.
translations.idiomatic: One year of servitude meant twenty days in the cangue, with five days added for each higher grade.

sentences.zh: 流二千里者，枷號五十日，每等亦遞加五日。

translations.literal: For exile two thousand li, wearing the cangue fifty days; each grade likewise adds five days.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li of exile meant fifty days in the cangue, again increasing by five days per grade.

sentences.zh: 充軍附近者，枷號七十日，近邊、沿海、邊外者八十日，極邊、煙瘴者九十日。

translations.literal: For nearby military banishment, wearing the cangue seventy days; for near frontier, coastal, and beyond-the-border banishment, eighty days; for extreme frontier and miasmic regions, ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby military banishment brought seventy days in the cangue; near border, coastal, and outer-border banishment eighty days; extreme border and miasmic regions ninety days.

sentences.zh: 」原立法之意，亦以旗人生則入檔，壯則充兵，鞏衛本根，未便離遠，有犯徒、流等罪，直以枷號代刑，強榦之義則然。

translations.literal: " The original intent of legislation was also that Bannermen were registered at birth and served as soldiers in maturity, consolidating and guarding their roots; it was not convenient to send them far away—when they committed penal servitude, exile, and the like, the cangue was used directly in place of punishment; such was the meaning of strengthening the trunk.
translations.idiomatic: The original idea was that Bannermen were registered at birth and mustered as soldiers in adulthood to guard the dynasty's foundation; they could not conveniently be sent far away, so the cangue substituted for exile or servitude—strengthening the trunk, as it were.

sentences.zh: 然犯系寡廉鮮恥，則銷除旗檔，一律實發，不姑息也。

translations.literal: Yet when the offense involved shameless conduct, their Banner register was struck off and they were actually sent into banishment without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: But offenses of brazen moral corruption led to removal from the Banner rolls and actual banishment without leniency.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜再犯加枷，初犯再犯計次加枷，犯奸加枷，賭博加枷，逃軍逃流加枷，暨一切敗檢逾閒、不顧行止者酌量加枷，則初無旗、民之別。

translations.literal: If repeat theft added the cangue, if first and repeat offenses were counted by number to add the cangue, if adultery added the cangue, gambling added the cangue, deserting soldiers and exiles added the cangue, and all who ruined their conduct and overstepped bounds without regard for propriety had the cangue added at discretion, then from the outset there was no distinction between Bannermen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat theft, counted repeat offenses, adultery, gambling, desertion from banishment or exile, and every kind of moral lapse could bring discretionary cangue time—with no distinction between Bannermen and civilians.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，部議囚禁人犯止用細鍊，不用長枷，而枷號遂專為行刑之用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Kangxi reign, the ministry deliberated that imprisoned convicts should use only light chains, not the long cangue, and wearing the cangue for a set term thus became exclusively a means of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669 the ministries ruled that jail prisoners should wear only light chains, not the long cangue, so cangue detention became purely a punitive sentence.

sentences.zh: 其數初不過一月、二月、三月，後竟有論年或永遠枷號者。

translations.literal: The duration at first was no more than one, two, or three months; later there were even terms counted in years or perpetual wearing of the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Terms began at one to three months but eventually stretched to years or even life in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 始制重者七十觔，輕者六十斤。

translations.literal: The initial regulation was seventy jin for the heavy and sixty jin for the light.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the heavy cangue weighed seventy jin and the light sixty.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，改定應枷人犯俱重二十五斤，然例尚有用百斤重枷者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Qianlong reign, it was changed so that all who should wear the cangue bore twenty-five jin; yet precedents still provided for a hundred-jin heavy cangue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1740 all cangues were standardized at twenty-five jin, though precedents still allowed hundred-jin heavy cangues.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以降，重枷斷用三十五斤，而於四川、陝西、湖北、河南、山東、安徽、廣東等省匪徒，又有系帶鐵杆石礅之例，亦一時創刑也。

translations.literal: From the Jiaqing reign onward, the heavy cangue was fixed at thirty-five jin; yet for bandits in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Guangdong, and other provinces there was also the precedent of attaching iron rods and stone blocks—a punitive innovation of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiaqing the heavy cangue was capped at thirty-five jin, but bandits in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Guangdong, and elsewhere could be shackled with iron rods and stone weights—another ad hoc punishment of the age.

sentences.zh: 刺字，古肉刑之一，律第嚴於賊盜。

translations.literal: Tattooing was one of the ancient corporal punishments; the code was strictest regarding thieves and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was an ancient corporal punishment; the code applied it most strictly to thieves and robbers.

sentences.zh: 乃其後條例滋多，刺緣坐，刺兇犯，刺逃軍、逃流，刺外遣、改遣、改發。

translations.literal: Later subsidiary rules multiplied: tattooing for guilt by association, tattooing violent offenders, tattooing deserters from military banishment and exile, tattooing those externally banished, re-banished, or re-assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Later subsidiary rules multiplied: tattoos for collective guilt, violent criminals, deserters from military banishment or exile, and those externally banished, re-banished, or re-assigned.

sentences.zh: 有刺事由者，有刺地方者，並有分刺滿、漢文字者。

translations.literal: Some tattoos recorded the cause of the offense, some the place, and some were divided between Manchu and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: Some marks recorded the offense, some the place of sentencing, and some used both Manchu and Chinese characters.

sentences.zh: 初刺右臂，次刺左臂，次刺右面、左面。

translations.literal: First the right arm was tattooed, then the left arm, then the right cheek and left cheek.
translations.idiomatic: The sequence was right arm, then left arm, then right cheek and left cheek.

sentences.zh: 大抵律多刺臂，例多刺面。

translations.literal: Generally the code mostly tattooed the arms, precedents mostly the face.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes tended to tattoo the arms; subsidiary rules tended to tattoo the face.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜責充警跡，二三年無過，或緝獲強盜二名以上、竊盜三名以上，例又准其起除刺字，復為良民。

translations.literal: If thieves were compelled to serve as police trackers, and for two or three years committed no offense, or captured two or more robbers or three or more thieves, precedents also permitted removing the tattoo and restoring them as good citizens.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves assigned as constabulary trackers who went two or three years without offense, or who captured two robbers or three thieves, could have their tattoos removed and regain good standing.

sentences.zh: 蓋惡惡雖嚴，而亦未嘗不予以自新之路焉。

translations.literal: Thus although hatred of evil was strict, a path to renewal was never wholly denied.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment of wrongdoing was severe, yet a path to reform was never wholly closed.

sentences.zh: 贖刑有三：一曰納贖，無力照律決配，有力照例納贖。

translations.literal: There are three forms of commutation by ransom: first, payment ransom—those without means are sentenced and assigned according to the code, those with means pay ransom according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation took three forms: payment ransom, for those with means who could buy off the statutory sentence while the poor were punished as the law required;

sentences.zh: 二曰收贖，老幼廢疾、天文生及婦人折杖，照律收贖。

translations.literal: second, collection ransom—the aged, young, disabled, students of astronomy, and women subject to commuted beating all paid collection ransom according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: collection ransom, for the aged, young, disabled, astronomy students, and women whose beating was commuted;

sentences.zh: 三曰贖罪，官員正妻及例難的決，並婦人有力者，照例贖罪。

translations.literal: third, offense ransom—principal wives of officials and cases where beating was hard to apply under precedent, as well as women with means, all paid offense ransom according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: and offense ransom, for officials' principal wives, cases where beating was impracticable, and women of means.

sentences.zh: 收贖名曰律贖，原本唐律收贖。

translations.literal: Collection ransom was called statutory ransom and originally derived from Tang law collection ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Collection ransom, called "statutory ransom," came straight from Tang law.

sentences.zh: 贖罪名為例贖，則明代所創行。

translations.literal: Offense ransom was called precedent ransom and was created and implemented by the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Offense ransom, or "precedent ransom," was a Ming innovation.

sentences.zh: 順治修律，五刑不列贖銀數目。

translations.literal: When the code was revised in the Shunzhi reign, the five punishments did not list amounts of ransom silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi code did not list ransom amounts for the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，始將明律贖圖內應贖銀數斟酌修改，定為納贖諸例圖。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Yongzheng reign, the amounts of ransom silver in the Ming code's ransom charts were carefully revised and fixed as charts for payment ransom and various precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 the Yongzheng court revised the Ming ransom tables and issued new charts for payment ransom.

sentences.zh: 然自康熙現行例定有承問官濫准納贖交部議處之條，而前明納贖及贖罪諸舊例又節經刪改，故律贖俱照舊援用，而例贖則多成具文。

translations.literal: Yet since the operative regulations of the Kangxi reign fixed a provision that examining officials who improperly permitted payment ransom were to be referred to the ministry for disciplinary action, and the old Ming precedents on payment ransom and offense ransom had been repeatedly revised and deleted, statutory ransom was all applied as before, while precedent ransom mostly became dead letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kangxi regulations punished officials who improperly allowed payment ransom, and many Ming payment- and offense-ransom precedents had been pared away—so statutory ransom continued in use while precedent ransom largely became a dead letter.

sentences.zh: 其捐贖一項，順治十八年，有官員犯流徒籍沒認工贖罪例；

translations.literal: As for the item of donated ransom, in the eighteenth year of the Shunzhi reign there was a precedent for officials guilty of exile or penal servitude whose property was confiscated to work off guilt by labor;
translations.idiomatic: Donated ransom appeared in many temporary forms: in 1661, officials sentenced to exile or servitude could work off sentences after confiscation;

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，有死罪現監人犯輸米邊口贖罪例；

translations.literal: in the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign, a precedent for death-row prisoners in custody to deliver grain to the frontier to ransom guilt;
translations.idiomatic: in 1690, death-row prisoners could deliver grain to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 三十年，有軍流人犯捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirtieth year, a precedent for military exiles and exiles to donate ransom;
translations.idiomatic: in 1691, military exiles and exiles could donate ransom;

sentences.zh: 三十四年，有通倉運米捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-fourth year, a precedent for transporting grain to the Tongcang granary to donate ransom;
translations.idiomatic: in 1695, convicts could ransom themselves by hauling grain to the Tongcang granary;

sentences.zh: 三十九年，有永定河工捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-ninth year, a precedent for donating ransom for Yongding River works;
translations.idiomatic: in 1700, by donating to Yongding River works;

sentences.zh: 六十年，有河工捐贖例。

translations.literal: in the sixtieth year, a precedent for donating ransom for river works.
translations.idiomatic: and in 1721, by donating to general river works.

sentences.zh: 然皆事竣停止，其歷朝沿用者，惟雍正十二年戶部會同刑部奏准預籌運糧事例，不論旗、民，罪應斬、絞，非常赦所不原者，三品以上官照西安駝捐例捐運糧銀一萬二千兩，四品官照營田例捐運糧銀五千兩，五、六品官照營田例捐銀四千兩，七品以下、進士、舉人二千五百兩，貢、監生二千兩，平人一千二百兩，軍、流各減十分之四，徒以下各減十分之六，俱准免罪。

translations.literal: Yet all ceased when the project ended; what was continued through successive reigns was only the precedent approved in the twelfth year of the Yongzheng reign by the Ministry of Revenue jointly with the Ministry of Justice for pre-paying transport grain: regardless of Bannerman or commoner, for offenses warranting decapitation or strangulation not pardoned by extraordinary amnesty, officials of the third rank and above donated twelve thousand taels of transport-grain silver according to the Xi'an camel-donation precedent; officials of the fourth rank five thousand taels according to the military-colony precedent; officials of the fifth and sixth ranks four thousand taels according to the military-colony precedent; those of the seventh rank and below, jinshi, and juren two thousand five hundred taels; tribute students and students of the Imperial Academy two thousand taels; commoners one thousand two hundred taels; military banishment and exile each reduced by four-tenths, penal servitude and below each reduced by six-tenths—all permitted to escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: All of these ended when the projects did. Only the 1734 precedent for pre-paying transport grain endured: Bannermen and civilians alike, for capital offenses not excluded from amnesty, could buy remission—twelve thousand taels for officials of third rank and above (per the Xi'an camel-donation scale), five thousand for fourth rank, four thousand for fifth and sixth, two thousand five hundred for seventh rank and below plus jinshi and juren, two thousand for tribute and academy students, twelve hundred for commoners, with military banishment and exile reduced forty percent and lesser sentences sixty percent.

sentences.zh: 西安駝捐，行自雍正元年，營田例則五年所定也。

translations.literal: The Xi'an camel donation had been in force since the first year of the Yongzheng reign; the military-colony precedent was fixed in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi'an camel-donation scale dated from 1723; the military-colony scale from 1727.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，西安布政使張若震奏請另定捐贖笞、杖銀數。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of the Qianlong reign, Zhang Ruozhen, financial commissioner of Xi'an, memorialized requesting separate fixation of donated-ransom silver amounts for beating with the light and heavy sticks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 Xi'an financial commissioner Zhang Ruozhen asked to set separate donated-ransom rates for light- and heavy-stick offenses.

sentences.zh: 經部議，預籌運糧事例，杖、笞與徒罪不分輕重，一例捐贖，究未允協。

translations.literal: After ministry deliberation, under the precedent for pre-paying transport grain, beating with the heavy and light sticks and penal servitude were not distinguished as to severity but were all alike subject to donated ransom—this was ultimately not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries replied that the transport-grain precedent treated light stick, heavy stick, and servitude alike without regard to severity, and that a uniform ransom rate was unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 除犯枷號、杖責者照徒罪捐贖外，酌擬分杖為一等，笞為一等。

translations.literal: Except for those guilty of wearing the cangue or subject to beating with the staff, who paid donated ransom according to penal servitude, it was proposed to divide heavy-stick beating into one grade and light-stick beating into one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from cangue offenders and those liable to staff beating, who ransomed themselves at servitude rates, the ministries proposed separate scales for heavy-stick and light-stick offenses.

sentences.zh: 其數，杖視徒遞減，笞視杖遞減。

translations.literal: The amounts decreased step by step from penal servitude for the staff, and from the staff for the light stick.
translations.idiomatic: Staff rates stepped down from servitude rates, and light-stick rates from staff rates.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諭將斬、絞緩決各犯納贖之例永行停止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an edict ordered that the precedent permitting payment ransom for all convicts under suspended decapitation or strangulation be permanently discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758 the throne ordered an end to ransom payments for prisoners awaiting autumn review on capital charges.

sentences.zh: 遇有恩赦減等時，其憚於遠行者，再准收贖。

translations.literal: When amnesty reduced sentences by grade, those who feared traveling far were again permitted collection ransom.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesties reduced sentences, those who dreaded long journeys could again pay collection ransom.

sentences.zh: 而贖鍰則仍視原擬罪名，不得照減等之罪。

translations.literal: Yet the ransom fine was still calculated according to the originally proposed offense and could not follow the reduced grade.
translations.idiomatic: The ransom sum, however, was still calculated on the original charge, not the reduced one.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: This was issued as an order.
translations.idiomatic: These rules were promulgated as statute.

sentences.zh: 嗣後官員贖罪者，俱照運糧事例核奪。

translations.literal: Thereafter all officials who ransomed offenses were assessed according to the transport-grain precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all officials who bought remission were assessed under the transport-grain scale.

sentences.zh: 刑部別設贖罪處，專司其事。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice separately established an office for offense ransom to handle the matter exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice set up a dedicated office to handle offense ransom.

sentences.zh: 此又律贖、例贖而外，別自為制者矣。

translations.literal: This was yet another system established apart from statutory ransom and precedent ransom.
translations.idiomatic: This was yet another system distinct from statutory and precedent ransom.

sentences.zh: 凌遲，用之十惡中不道以上諸重罪，號為極刑。

translations.literal: Lingchi was applied to grave offenses from "unnatural conduct" upward among the Ten Abominations and was called the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchi applied to the gravest offenses among the Ten Abominations from "unnatural conduct" upward and was called the supreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 梟首，則強盜居多。

translations.literal: Exposure of the head was mostly applied to robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying the head was chiefly reserved for robbers.

sentences.zh: 戮屍，所以待惡逆及強盜應梟諸犯之監故者。

translations.literal: Dismemberment of the corpse was used for those guilty of treason and for robbers who should have been exposed but died in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse mutilation punished treason and robbers who should have been displayed but died in prison.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸刑，類皆承用明律，略有通變，行之二百餘年。

translations.literal: All these punishments largely followed the Ming code, with slight adaptations, and were in force for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: These punishments largely followed Ming law with minor Qing adjustments and remained in force for more than two centuries.

sentences.zh: 至過誤殺之賠人，竊盜之割腳筋，重辟減等之貫耳鼻，強盜、貪官及窩逃之籍家產，或沿自盛京定例，或順治朝偶行之峻令，不久革除，非所論也。

translations.literal: As for compensation for accidental killing, cutting the tendons of the heel for theft, piercing the ears and nose when reducing grave penalties by grade, confiscating household property for robbers, corrupt officials, and harborers of fugitives—some derived from regulations fixed at Mukden, some were harsh orders occasionally enforced in the Shunzhi reign and soon abolished—these are not discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: Compensation for accidental homicide, cutting heel tendons for theft, piercing ears and nose when commuting capital sentences, and confiscating the property of robbers, corrupt officials, and harborers of fugitives—some from Mukden regulations, some harsh Shunzhi experiments soon repealed—lie outside this survey.

sentences.zh: 自光緒變法，二十八年，山西巡撫趙爾巽奏請各省通設罪犯習藝所。

translations.literal: From the Guangxu legal reforms, in the twenty-eighth year, Shanxi governor Zhao Erxun memorialized requesting that every province establish workhouses for convicts to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reforms, in 1902 Shanxi governor Zhao Erxun asked every province to establish vocational workhouses for convicts.

sentences.zh: 經刑部議准，徒犯毋庸發配，按照年限，於本地收所習藝。

translations.literal: After deliberation the Ministry of Justice approved: convicts sentenced to penal servitude need not be sent away but, according to the term, were received in local workhouses to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice approved: servitude convicts would no longer be sent away but held locally in workhouses for the statutory term.

sentences.zh: 軍、流為常赦所不原者，照定例發配，到配一律收所習藝。

translations.literal: Military banishment and exile not pardoned by regular amnesty were assigned according to fixed precedent; upon arrival all were received in workhouses to learn trades.
translations.idiomatic: Military banishment and exile excluded from regular amnesty were still assigned as before, but upon arrival all entered workhouses.

sentences.zh: 流二千里限工作六年，二千五百里八年，三千里者十年。

translations.literal: Exile two thousand li was limited to six years of labor, two thousand five hundred li to eight years, three thousand li to ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li of exile meant six years' labor, two thousand five hundred eight years, and three thousand ten years.

sentences.zh: 遣軍照滿流年限計算，限滿釋放，聽其自謀生計，並准在配所入籍為民。

translations.literal: Banishment dispatch and military banishment were calculated according to the term for full exile; when the term expired they were released, allowed to seek their own livelihood, and permitted to register as commoners at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment dispatch and military banishment followed full-exile terms; when terms expired convicts were released, free to make a living and register as civilians at their place of assignment.

sentences.zh: 若為常赦所得原者，無論軍、流，俱無庸發配，即在本省收所習藝。

translations.literal: If pardoned by regular amnesty, whether military banishment or exile, none needed to be sent away but were received in workhouses within their own province.
translations.idiomatic: Those covered by regular amnesty, whether military banishment or exile, were not sent away but held in provincial workhouses.

sentences.zh: 工作年限，亦照前科算。

translations.literal: The term of labor was likewise calculated as before.
translations.idiomatic: Labor terms were calculated as above.

sentences.zh: 自此五徒並不發配，即軍、流之發配者，數亦銳減矣。

translations.literal: From this time the five grades of penal servitude were no longer sent away; even those military banishments and exiles who were assigned sharply decreased in number.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the five servitude grades were never sent away, and even assigned military banishments and exiles dropped sharply in number.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，刑部奏准刪除充軍名目，將附近、近邊，邊遠併入三流，極邊及煙瘴改為安置，仍與當差並行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of Justice memorialized and was approved to delete the category of military banishment, merging nearby and near frontier and distant frontier into the three grades of exile, changing extreme frontier and miasmic regions to resettlement, still parallel with performing duty.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 the Ministry of Justice abolished military banishment as a category, folding nearby, near border, and distant border into the three exile grades and recasting extreme border and miasmic regions as resettlement, while retaining labor duty.

sentences.zh: 自此五軍第留其二，而刑名亦改變矣。

translations.literal: From this time only two of the five military categories remained, and the nomenclature of punishments also changed.
translations.idiomatic: Only two of the five former military grades survived, and penal terminology shifted again.

sentences.zh: 三十年，劉坤一、張之洞會奏變法第二摺內，有恤刑獄九條。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, in the joint memorial on reforms, second memorial, by Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong, there were nine articles on leniency in prisons and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904 Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong's joint reform memorial included nine articles on leniency in criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 其省刑責條內，經法律館議准，笞、杖等罪，仿照外國罰金之法，改為罰銀。

translations.literal: Within the article on reducing corporal punishment, the Law Codification Bureau deliberated and approved changing offenses of beating with the light and heavy sticks, following foreign fine laws, to fines in silver.
translations.idiomatic: Under the article on reducing corporal punishment, the Law Codification Bureau approved replacing light- and heavy-stick beating with silver fines modeled on Western practice.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內笞刑五，以五錢為一等，至笞五十罰銀二兩五錢，杖六十者改為罰五兩。

translations.literal: For the five grades of beating with the light stick in statutes and precedents, five cash per grade, up to fifty blows of the light stick fined two taels five mace of silver; sixty blows of the heavy stick was changed to a fine of five taels.
translations.idiomatic: The five light-stick grades were set at five cash per grade, up to fifty strokes at two taels five mace; sixty heavy strokes became a five-tael fine.

sentences.zh: 每一等加二兩五錢，以次遞加，至杖一百改為罰十五兩而止。

translations.literal: Each grade added two taels five mace, increasing step by step, up to one hundred blows of the heavy stick changed to a fine of fifteen taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each higher grade added two taels five mace, topping out at one hundred heavy strokes converted to fifteen taels.

sentences.zh: 如無力完納，折為作工。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, it was converted to labor.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay could work off the fine.

sentences.zh: 應罰一兩，折作工四日，以次遞加，至十五兩折作工六十日而止。

translations.literal: One tael due was converted to four days of labor, increasing step by step, up to fifteen taels converted to sixty days of labor.
translations.idiomatic: One tael equaled four days' labor, scaling up to fifteen taels for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 然竊盜未便罰金，議將犯竊應擬笞罪者，改科工作一月；

translations.literal: Yet theft was not convenient to punish with fines; it was proposed that those guilty of theft who should receive beating with the light stick be changed to one month of labor;
translations.idiomatic: Theft, however, was not suited to fines; thieves who would have received light-stick sentences were instead assigned one month's labor;

sentences.zh: 杖六十者，改科工作兩月；

translations.literal: sixty blows of the heavy stick to two months of labor;
translations.idiomatic: sixty heavy strokes to two months;

sentences.zh: 杖七十至一百，每等遞加兩月。

translations.literal: from seventy to one hundred blows of the heavy stick, each grade adding two months.
translations.idiomatic: and from seventy to one hundred strokes, two months added per grade.

sentences.zh: 又附片請將軍、流、徒加杖概予寬免，無庸決責。

translations.literal: A supplementary memorial also requested that supplementary beating for military banishment, exile, and penal servitude be wholly remitted, with no need for execution of blows.
translations.idiomatic: A supplementary memorial also asked to abolish supplementary beating for military banishment, exile, and servitude.

sentences.zh: 自此而笞、杖二刑廢棄矣。

translations.literal: From this time the two punishments of beating with the light and heavy sticks were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Light- and heavy-stick beating were thus abolished.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，修訂法律大臣沈家本等奏請刪除重法數端，略稱：「見行律例款目極繁，而最重之法，亟應先議刪除者，約有三事：一曰凌遲、梟首、戮屍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the revising law ministers Shen Jiaben and others memorialized requesting deletion of several heavy penalties, stating in summary: "The articles of the current statutes and precedents are extremely numerous, and among the heaviest penalties those that should first be discussed for deletion are roughly three matters: first, lingchi, exposure of the head, and dismemberment of the corpse."
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 revising law minister Shen Jiaben and colleagues memorialized to abolish several harsh penalties, observing: "Current statutes and precedents are vast, but three supreme punishments should be removed first: lingchi, displaying the head, and corpse mutilation."

sentences.zh: 凌遲之刑，唐以前無此名目。

translations.literal: The penalty of lingchi had no such name before the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchi did not exist before the Tang.

sentences.zh: 遼史刑法志始列入正刑之內。

translations.literal: The penal monograph of the History of Liao first listed it among the regular punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao penal code first listed it among regular punishments.

sentences.zh: 宋自熙寧以後，漸亦沿用。

translations.literal: From the Xining reign of the Song onward it was gradually adopted as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Song adopted it gradually after the Xining era.

sentences.zh: 元、明至今，相仍未改。

translations.literal: From Yuan and Ming down to the present it has continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Ming, and Qing kept it without change.

sentences.zh: 梟首在秦、漢時惟用諸夷族之誅，六朝梁、陳、齊、周諸律，始於斬之外別立梟名。

translations.literal: Exposure of the head in Qin and Han was used only for the extermination of alien clans; the codes of Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou in the Six Dynasties first established the name of exposure apart from decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin and Han, displaying the head applied only to clan extermination; the Six Dynasties codes of Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou first named it as a punishment separate from decapitation.

sentences.zh: 自隋迄元，復棄而不用。

translations.literal: From Sui through Yuan it was again abandoned and not used.
translations.idiomatic: From Sui through Yuan it fell out of use.

sentences.zh: 今之斬梟，仍明制也。

translations.literal: Today's decapitation with exposure still follows the Ming system.
translations.idiomatic: Today's beheading with display of the head still follows Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 戮屍一事，惟秦時成蟜軍反，其軍吏皆斬戮屍，見於始皇本紀。

translations.literal: As for dismemberment of the corpse, only when Prince Cheng Jiao's army rebelled in Qin were its officers all decapitated and their corpses dismembered, as seen in the Basic Annals of the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse mutilation appears only once in antiquity: when Prince Cheng Jiao rebelled in Qin, his officers were beheaded and their corpses dismembered, as recorded in the First Emperor's annals.

sentences.zh: 此外歷代刑制，俱無此法。

translations.literal: Apart from this, penal systems of successive dynasties all lacked this law.
translations.idiomatic: No other dynasty's penal code included this punishment.

sentences.zh: 明自萬曆十六年，定有戮屍條例，專指謀殺祖父母、父母而言。

translations.literal: From the sixteenth year of Wanli in the Ming, a precedent on dismemberment of the corpse was fixed, referring specifically to plotting to kill grandparents and parents.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming fixed a corpse-mutilation rule in 1588 specifically for plotting to murder grandparents or parents.

sentences.zh: 國朝因之，後更推及於強盜。

translations.literal: Our dynasty followed it, and later extended it to robbers as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing followed suit and later extended it to robbers.

sentences.zh: 凡此酷重之刑，固所以懲戒兇惡。

translations.literal: All these cruel and heavy penalties were indeed meant to punish the vicious and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: These savage punishments were meant to deter the vicious.

sentences.zh: 第刑至於斬，身首分離，已為至慘。

translations.literal: Yet when punishment reaches decapitation, with body and head separated, it is already the utmost cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beheading already separates body and head—the utmost cruelty.

sentences.zh: 若命在頃忽，菹醢必令備嘗，氣久消亡，刀鋸猶難倖免，揆諸仁人之心，當必慘然不樂。

translations.literal: If life ends in an instant, yet mincing and dismemberment must all be tasted; when breath has long ceased, knife and saw still cannot be escaped—measured by the heart of a humane person, this must surely inspire grief and displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: If death comes in an instant, yet the victim must still endure dismemberment; when breath is long gone, the knife and saw still cannot be spared—any humane mind must recoil in horror.

sentences.zh: 謂將以懲本犯，而被刑者魂魄何知；

translations.literal: If it is said to punish the principal offender, what would the executed person's soul know?
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to punish the offender, what can a dead man's spirit know?

sentences.zh: 謂將以警戒眾人，而習見習聞，轉感召其殘忍之性，實非聖世所宜遵。

translations.literal: If it is said to warn the multitude, yet through constant seeing and hearing it instead summons their cruel nature—this is truly not what a sage age should follow.
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to warn the public, habitual exposure only breeds cruelty—hardly fitting for an enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 請將凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項，一概刪除，死罪至斬決而止。

translations.literal: We request that lingchi, exposure of the head, and dismemberment of the corpse be wholly deleted, with death penalties stopping at decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that lingchi, displaying the head, and corpse mutilation be abolished altogether, with capital punishment ending at beheading.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改斬決。

translations.literal: All articles on lingchi and decapitation with exposure in statutes and precedents should be changed to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: All statutory articles calling for lingchi or beheading with display should be changed to simple beheading.

sentences.zh: 斬決而下，依次遞減。

translations.literal: Below decapitation, reduce step by step in order.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser penalties should be stepped down accordingly.

sentences.zh: 一曰緣坐。

translations.literal: Second, guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Second, collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 緣坐之制，起於秦之參夷及收司連坐法。

translations.literal: The system of guilt by association arose from Qin practices of implicating clans and collective punishment of those connected in office.
translations.idiomatic: Collective punishment began with Qin clan extermination and office-linked joint liability.

sentences.zh: 漢高後除三族令，文帝除收孥相坐律，當時以為盛德。

translations.literal: Empress Gao of Han abolished the order on the three clans; Emperor Wen abolished the law on imprisoning relatives for collective guilt—at the time these were considered great virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü abolished the three-clan extermination; Emperor Wen ended the law imprisoning relatives for joint guilt—both hailed as great acts of mercy.

sentences.zh: 惜夷族之誅，猶間用之。

translations.literal: Regrettably, extermination of clans was still occasionally used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet clan extermination was still used from time to time.

sentences.zh: 晉以下仍有家屬從坐之法，唐律惟反叛、惡逆、不道，律有緣坐，他無有也。

translations.literal: From Jin downward there were still laws on family members sharing punishment; Tang law had guilt by association only for rebellion, treason, and unnatural conduct—nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and later dynasties still punished families; Tang law allowed collective punishment only for rebellion, treason, and unnatural conduct.

sentences.zh: 今律則奸黨、交結近侍諸項俱緣坐矣，反獄、邪教諸項亦緣坐矣。

translations.literal: Today's code implicates associates in factionalism and collusion with palace attendants, and also implicates associates in prison revolt and heterodox sects.
translations.idiomatic: Today's code implicates associates in factionalism, collusion with palace attendants, prison revolt, and heterodox sects alike.

sentences.zh: 一案株連，動輒數十人。

translations.literal: One case could implicate dozens of people.
translations.idiomatic: A single case could drag in dozens of people.

sentences.zh: 夫以一人之故而波及全家，以無罪之人而科以重罪，漢文帝以為不正之法反害於民，北魏崔挺嘗曰『一人有罪，延及闔門，則司馬牛受桓魋之罰，柳下惠膺盜跖之誅，不亦哀哉』，其言皆篤論也。

translations.literal: For one person's offense to engulf the whole family, for innocent persons to receive heavy punishment—Emperor Wen of Han held that unjust laws harm the people; Cui Ting of Northern Wei once said, "When one man is guilty and the whole household is implicated, then Sima Niu suffers Huan Tui's punishment and Liuxia Hui bears Zhi the Robber's execution—is this not lamentable?"—all sound judgments.
translations.idiomatic: To punish an entire family for one person's crime, to impose heavy sentences on the innocent—Emperor Wen called such laws harmful; Cui Ting of Northern Wei said: "When one man sins and the whole household suffers, Sima Niu pays for Huan Tui's crime and Liuxia Hui dies for Robber Zhi—how lamentable!"—sound words both.

sentences.zh: 今世各國，皆主持刑罰止及一身之義，與『罪人不孥』之古訓實相符合。

translations.literal: All nations today uphold the principle that punishment applies only to the person himself, which truly accords with the ancient teaching that "the guilty do not implicate their children."
translations.idiomatic: Modern nations hold that punishment should fall on the offender alone—a principle that matches the ancient teaching that guilt does not extend to one's family.

sentences.zh: 請將律內緣坐各條，除知情者仍坐罪外，其不知情者悉予寬免。

translations.literal: We request that all articles on guilt by association in the code, except that those who knew the facts should still be punished, all who did not know be wholly exempted.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that collective-punishment articles be revised so that only those who knew the facts are punished and the ignorant are spared.

sentences.zh: 餘條有科及家屬者准此。

translations.literal: Other articles that impose punishment on family members should follow this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Other articles punishing family members should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 一曰刺字。

translations.literal: Third, tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Third, tattooing.

sentences.zh: 刺字乃古墨刑，漢之黥也。

translations.literal: Tattooing is the ancient ink punishment, the branding of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was the ancient ink punishment—the Han branding penalty.

sentences.zh: 文帝廢肉刑而黥亦廢，魏、晉、六朝雖有逃奴劫盜之刺，旋行旋廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishments and branding was abolished as well; Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties sometimes tattooed fugitive slaves and robbers, but the practice was adopted and abandoned in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishment and branding with it; Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties occasionally tattooed fugitive slaves and robbers, but the practice was repeatedly adopted and dropped.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐皆無此法。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang both lacked this law.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Tang law had no such provision.

sentences.zh: 至石晉天福間，始創刺配之制，相沿至今。

translations.literal: Only in the Tianfu era of Later Jin was the system of tattooing and assignment first created, continuing to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Later Jin Tianfu era was tattooing combined with banishment introduced, and it has continued ever since.

sentences.zh: 其初不過竊盜逃人，其後日加煩密。

translations.literal: At first it applied only to thieves and fugitives; later it grew daily more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: At first it applied only to thieves and fugitives; later it grew ever more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 在立法之意，原欲使莠民知恥，庶幾悔過而遷善。

translations.literal: In the intent of legislation, it was originally meant to make wicked people feel shame, so that they might repent and turn to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The original intent was to shame wrongdoers into repentance and reform.

sentences.zh: 詎知習於為非者，適予以標識，助其兇橫。

translations.literal: Who would have known that those accustomed to wrongdoing would instead be given a mark that aided their ferocity?
translations.idiomatic: Yet habitual offenders treated the mark as a badge that encouraged their brutality.

sentences.zh: 而偶罹法網者，則黥刺一膺，終身僇辱。

translations.literal: Those who chanced to fall into the net of the law, once branded once, suffered lifelong shame.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stumbled into the law once bore a lifelong mark of disgrace.

sentences.zh: 夫肉刑久廢，而此法獨存，漢文所謂刻肌膚痛而不德者，未能收弼教之益，而徒留此不德之名，豈仁政所宜出此。

translations.literal: Corporal punishment was long abolished, yet this law alone survived; what Emperor Wen of Han called cutting the flesh and causing pain without virtue—unable to obtain the benefit of assisting instruction, it only left this name without virtue. How could humane governance produce this?
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was abolished long ago, yet tattooing alone survived. Emperor Wen called such punishments pain without virtue—they do not reform but only leave an indelible stain. How can humane government tolerate them?

sentences.zh: 擬請將刺字款目，概行刪除。

translations.literal: It is proposed to delete all articles on tattooing entirely.
translations.idiomatic: We propose abolishing all tattooing provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡竊盜皆令收所習藝，按罪名輕重，定以年限，俾一技能嫻，得以餬口，自少再犯、三犯之人。

translations.literal: All thieves should be received in workhouses to learn trades, with terms fixed according to the severity of the offense, so that once skilled in a craft they can support themselves—thus reducing repeat and third-time offenders.
translations.idiomatic: All thieves should enter workhouses for terms fixed by offense severity, learn a trade, and support themselves—thereby reducing repeat offenders.

sentences.zh: 一切遞解人犯，嚴令地方官僉差押解，果能實力奉行，逃亡者自少也。

translations.literal: For all convicts escorted under guard, local officials should be strictly ordered to assign escorts for delivery; if this were truly enforced, fugitives would naturally be few.
translations.idiomatic: If local officials strictly assigned reliable escorts for all transported convicts, escapes would become rare.

sentences.zh: 」奏上，諭令凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項永遠刪除。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered the three items of lingchi, exposure of the head, and dismemberment of the corpse permanently deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved, and an edict permanently abolished lingchi, displaying the head, and corpse mutilation.

sentences.zh: 所有現行律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改為斬決；

translations.literal: All current articles on lingchi and decapitation with exposure were changed to decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: All articles calling for lingchi or beheading with display were changed to simple beheading;

sentences.zh: 其斬決各條，俱改為絞決；

translations.literal: all articles on decapitation were changed to strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: all immediate-beheading articles were changed to immediate strangulation;

sentences.zh: 絞決各條，俱改為絞監候，入於秋審情實；

translations.literal: all articles on strangulation were changed to strangulation awaiting review, entering the confirmed cases of autumn review;
translations.idiomatic: all immediate-strangulation articles were changed to strangulation awaiting autumn review;

sentences.zh: 斬監候各條，俱改為絞監候，與絞候人犯仍入於秋審，分別實緩。

translations.literal: all articles on decapitation awaiting review were changed to strangulation awaiting review; together with those awaiting strangulation they still entered autumn review, classified as confirmed or reprieved.
translations.idiomatic: all beheading-awaiting-review articles became strangulation awaiting review; all such prisoners still entered autumn review, classified as confirmed or reprieved.

sentences.zh: 至緣坐各條，除知情者仍治罪外，餘悉寬免。

translations.literal: As for articles on guilt by association, except that those who knew were still punished, the rest were all exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Collective-punishment articles were revised: only those who knew were punished; the rest were spared.

sentences.zh: 其刺字等項，亦概行革除。

translations.literal: Tattooing and similar items were also wholly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing and similar punishments were abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 旨下，中外稱頌焉。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, within and without the realm there was praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree was issued, praise resounded throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，法律館奏准將戲殺、誤殺、擅殺虛擬死罪各案，分別減為徒、流。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the Law Codification Bureau memorialized and was approved to reduce cases of killing in sport, accidental killing, and unauthorized killing with fictitiously imposed death penalties, respectively, to penal servitude and exile.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 the Law Codification Bureau approved reducing sport killing, accidental killing, and unauthorized killing cases from nominal capital offenses to servitude or exile.

sentences.zh: 自此而死刑亦多輕減矣。

translations.literal: From this time death penalties were also largely lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was thus further lightened.

sentences.zh: 又是年法律館以婦女收贖，銀數太微，不足以資警戒，議准婦女犯笞、杖，照新章罰金。

translations.literal: Also in that year the Law Codification Bureau held that collection ransom for women, with silver amounts too small, was insufficient for warning; it was approved that women guilty of beating with the light or heavy stick should pay fines according to the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Bureau found women's collection-ransom amounts too small to deter offense and approved fines under the new regulations for women guilty of light- or heavy-stick offenses.

sentences.zh: 徒、流、軍、遣，除不孝及奸、盜、詐偽舊例應實發者，改留本地習藝所工作，以十年為限，餘俱准其贖罪。

translations.literal: For penal servitude, exile, military banishment, and banishment dispatch, except unfilial conduct and adultery, theft, and fraud under old precedents requiring actual assignment, they were changed to remain in local workhouses for labor, with ten years as the limit; the rest were all permitted offense ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Servitude, exile, military banishment, and banishment dispatch—except unfilial conduct, adultery, theft, and fraud requiring actual assignment—were commuted to ten years' labor in local workhouses; all others could pay offense ransom.

sentences.zh: 徒一年折銀二十兩，每五兩為一等，五徒准此遞加。

translations.literal: One year of penal servitude was converted to twenty taels of silver, five taels per grade, the five grades of servitude increasing accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: One year of servitude equaled twenty taels of silver, increasing by five taels per grade through all five servitude grades.

sentences.zh: 由徒入流，每一等加十兩，三流准此遞加。

translations.literal: From servitude into exile, each grade added ten taels, the three grades of exile increasing accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: From servitude into exile, each grade added ten taels through all three exile grades.

sentences.zh: 遣、軍照滿流科斷。

translations.literal: Banishment dispatch and military banishment were sentenced according to full exile.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment dispatch and military banishment were assessed at full-exile rates.

sentences.zh: 如無力完繳，將應罰之數，照新章按銀數折算時日，改習工藝。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, the amount due was converted to days according to the new regulations by silver amount, changed to learning crafts.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay could work off the sum in vocational labor at the rates set by the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 其犯該枷號，不論日數多寡，俱酌加五兩，以示區別。

translations.literal: Those liable to wearing the cangue, regardless of the number of days, all had five taels added at discretion to show distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue sentences, regardless of duration, carried an additional five-tael surcharge.

sentences.zh: 自此而收贖銀數亦稍變矣。

translations.literal: From this time collection-ransom silver amounts also changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Collection-ransom amounts shifted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 故宣統二年頒布之現行刑律，第將近數年奏定之章程採獲修入，於是刑制遂大有變更。

translations.literal: Thus the current penal code promulgated in the second year of Xuantong merely incorporated regulations memorialized and approved in recent years; thereby the penal system underwent great change.
translations.idiomatic: The penal code promulgated in 1910 incorporated regulations approved in recent years, and the penal system was transformed.

sentences.zh: 其五刑之目，首罰刑十，以代舊律之笞、杖。

translations.literal: Among the categories of the five punishments, the first was ten grades of fine punishment, replacing the beating with light and heavy sticks of the old code.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five punishments, ten grades of fines replaced the old light- and heavy-stick beating.

sentences.zh: 一等罰，罰銀五錢，至十等罰，為銀十五兩，據法律館議覆恤刑獄之奏也。

translations.literal: The first grade of fine was five mace of silver in fine; up to the tenth grade of fine, fifteen taels of silver—according to the Law Codification Bureau's deliberative reply to the memorial on leniency in prisons and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The first fine grade was five mace of silver; the tenth fifteen taels—per the Law Codification Bureau's reply to the memorial on leniency in criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 次徒刑五，年限仍舊律。

translations.literal: Next came the five grades of penal servitude, with terms still following the old code.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the five grades of penal servitude, with terms unchanged from the old code.

sentences.zh: 次流刑三，道里仍舊律，然均不加杖，以法律館業經附片奏刪也。

translations.literal: Next came the three grades of exile, with distances still following the old code, yet none with additional beating, because the Law Codification Bureau had already memorialized in a supplementary document to delete this.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the three exile grades at the old distances, but without supplementary beating—the Law Codification Bureau had already secured its abolition.

sentences.zh: 次遣刑二：曰極邊足四千里及煙瘴地方安置，曰新疆當差。

translations.literal: Next came two grades of banishment dispatch: resettlement at the extreme frontier of four thousand li and miasmic regions, and performing duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Next came two banishment-dispatch grades: resettlement at the extreme frontier or in miasmic regions, and labor duty in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 以閏刑加入正刑，承用者廣，不得不別自為制也。

translations.literal: Because intercalary punishments were added to the regular punishments and widely applied, they had to be made a separate system.
translations.idiomatic: Because these supplementary punishments had been folded into regular practice so widely, they required a separate statutory category.

sentences.zh: 次死刑二：曰絞，曰斬。

translations.literal: Next came two death penalties: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Finally came two capital punishments: strangulation and beheading.

sentences.zh: 時雖有死刑唯一之議，以舊制顯分等差，且凌遲、梟首等項甫經議減，不敢徑行廢斬也。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of a single death penalty, but because the old system clearly distinguished grades, and lingchi, exposure of the head, and similar items had only just been discussed for reduction, they did not dare directly abolish decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued for a single form of capital punishment, but the old system clearly distinguished grades, and with lingchi and display of the head only just abolished, beheading could not be discarded outright.

sentences.zh: 徒、流雖仍舊律，然為制不同。

translations.literal: Although penal servitude and exile still followed the old code, the system of implementation differed.
translations.idiomatic: Servitude and exile kept the old statutory labels but worked differently in practice.

sentences.zh: 按照習藝章程，五徒依限收入本地習藝所習藝；

translations.literal: According to the regulations on learning trades, the five grades of penal servitude were received within the term in local workhouses to learn trades;
translations.idiomatic: Under the vocational-workhouse regulations, all five servitude grades were held locally for the statutory term;

sentences.zh: 流、遣毋論發配與否，俱應工作。

translations.literal: for exile and banishment dispatch, whether or not sent to assignment, all were required to labor.
translations.idiomatic: exiles and banishment-dispatch convicts, whether or not sent away, were all required to work.

sentences.zh: 故於徒五等註明按限工作，流二千里注工作六年，二千五百里注工作八年，三千里注工作十年，遣刑俱注工作十二年。

translations.literal: Therefore for the five grades of penal servitude it was noted to labor within the term; for exile two thousand li, six years of labor; two thousand five hundred li, eight years; three thousand li, ten years; for banishment dispatch, all noted twelve years of labor.
translations.idiomatic: The code therefore specified labor terms for each servitude grade, six years for two thousand li of exile, eight for two thousand five hundred, ten for three thousand, and twelve for banishment dispatch.

sentences.zh: 收贖則根據婦女贖罪新章酌減銀數，改為通例。

translations.literal: Collection ransom, based on the new regulations on women's offense ransom with reduced silver amounts, was changed into a general rule.
translations.idiomatic: Collection-ransom amounts were reduced on the model of the new women's-ransom regulations and made a general rule.

sentences.zh: 罰刑照應罰之數折半收贖，徒一年贖銀十兩，每等加銀二兩五錢，至徒三年收贖銀二十兩。

translations.literal: Fine punishment was collected at half the amount due; one year of penal servitude ransomed for ten taels of silver, each grade adding two taels five mace, up to three years of penal servitude collected at twenty taels.
translations.idiomatic: Fines could be commuted at half the assessed amount; one year of servitude cost ten taels, increasing by two taels five mace per grade to twenty taels for three years.

sentences.zh: 流刑每等加銀五兩，至三千里贖銀三十五兩。

translations.literal: For exile each grade added five taels of silver, up to three thousand li at thirty-five taels.
translations.idiomatic: Each exile grade added five taels, up to thirty-five taels for three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 遣刑與滿流同科。

translations.literal: Banishment dispatch was sentenced on the same scale as full exile.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment dispatch was assessed at the full-exile rate.

sentences.zh: 絞、斬則收贖銀四十兩。

translations.literal: Strangulation and decapitation were collected at forty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation and beheading could be commuted for forty taels.

sentences.zh: 亦分注於各刑條下。

translations.literal: These were also noted separately under each penal article.
translations.idiomatic: These amounts were noted under each relevant article.

sentences.zh: 然非例應收贖者，不得濫及也。

translations.literal: Yet those not eligible for collection ransom by precedent could not be extended to indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Only those statutorily eligible could claim collection ransom.

sentences.zh: 捐贖，據光緒二十九年刑部奏准照運糧事例，減半銀數，另輯為例。

translations.literal: Donated ransom, according to the Ministry of Justice memorial approved in the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu following the transport-grain precedent with halved silver amounts, was separately compiled as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Donated ransom followed the 1903 Ministry of Justice approval of halved transport-grain rates, compiled as a separate precedent.

sentences.zh: 其笞、杖雖不入正刑，仍留竹板，以備刑訊之用。

translations.literal: Although beating with the light and heavy sticks was no longer among the regular punishments, bamboo boards were retained for use in judicial torture.
translations.idiomatic: Light- and heavy-stick beating was no longer a regular punishment, but bamboo boards were kept for interrogation under torture.

sentences.zh: 外此各刑具，盡行廢除，枷號亦一概芟削，刑制較為徑省矣。

translations.literal: Apart from this, all other penal implements were wholly abolished, and wearing the cangue was also entirely cut away—the penal system became rather more direct and economical.
translations.idiomatic: All other penal implements were abolished, cangue detention eliminated altogether, and the system became considerably simpler.

sentences.zh: 惟就地正法一項，始自咸豐三年。

translations.literal: Only the item of summary execution on the spot began in the third year of the Xianfeng reign.
translations.idiomatic: Only summary execution on the spot, introduced in 1853, remained.

sentences.zh: 時各省軍興，地方大吏，遇土匪竊發，往往先行正法，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: At that time military campaigns arose in the provinces; local grandees, encountering bandits and thieves breaking out, often executed them on the spot first and then reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion spread across the provinces, local governors often executed bandits on the spot and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 嗣軍務敉平，疆吏樂其便己，相沿不改。

translations.literal: Later, when military affairs were pacified, frontier officials found it convenient for themselves and continued the practice unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars ended, frontier officials found the practice convenient and kept it up.

sentences.zh: 光緒七八年間，御史胡隆洵、陳啟泰等屢以為言。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Guangxu, censors Hu Longxun, Chen Qitai, and others repeatedly spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881–1882 censors Hu Longxun, Chen Qitai, and others repeatedly protested.

sentences.zh: 刑部聲請飭下各省，體察情形，仍照舊例解勘，分別題奏。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice requested orders sent down to the provinces to investigate local conditions and still, according to the old precedent, forward cases for examination and report them separately in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice asked the provinces to investigate and restore the old procedure of forwarding cases for review and memorializing separately.

sentences.zh: 嗣各督撫俱覆稱地方不靖，礙難規復舊制。

translations.literal: Later all governors-general and governors replied that local conditions were unsettled and it was difficult to restore the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Every governor replied that local conditions were too unsettled to restore the old system.

sentences.zh: 刑部不得已，乃酌量加以限制，如實系土匪、馬賊、游勇、會匪，方准先行正法，尋常強盜，不得濫引。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice, having no alternative, then limited the practice at discretion: only if they were truly bandits, horse bandits, roaming soldiers, or secret-society members might summary execution on the spot be permitted; ordinary robbers could not be cited indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice reluctantly limited the practice: only genuine bandits, mounted brigands, roaming soldiers, or secret-society members could be summarily executed; ordinary robbers could not be included.

sentences.zh: 自此章程行，沿及國變，而就地正法之制，訖未之能革。

translations.literal: From the time this regulation was enforced, continuing through the change of dynasty, the system of summary execution on the spot was never abolished to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Once this regulation took effect, it continued through the fall of the dynasty, and summary execution on the spot was never abolished.
